claims.explanation: SC-9 is a naphthalenesulfonamide PKC activator that kills cells dependent on PKC signaling, and the selective pattern tracks with intact PKC-pathway signaling rather than a single lineage. Lines with PTEN loss (which elevates PKC/PI3K signaling) and RAS/BRAF activation are enriched among sensitive lines, while lines with PIK3CA mutation, NRAS mutation, or high EGFR/MAP2K1-driven signaling are relatively protected, suggesting that SC-9 sensitivity reflects PKC-dependent survival signaling that is bypassed by alternative PI3K/MAPK activation.

features.basis: PTEN loss elevates PKC/PI3K signaling; enriched in sensitive lines (UACC62, FTC133, KALS1, 786O)
TP53 mutation is near-universal in sensitive lines and absent in several resistant lines
BRAF-mutant melanomas (UACC62, K029AX, LOXIMVI) are among the most killed
KRAS-mutant lines (OV7, KPNSI9S, CL11) appear in the sensitive set
PIK3CA-mutant lines (HGC27, KYSE510, SNUC5, SNU840) are enriched among least affected
NRAS-mutant lines (IPC298, KU1919) are among the least affected
EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines (NCIH1650, HCC4006) are relatively resistant
MAP2K1-mutant NCIH1437 is among the least affected lines
SC-9 activates PKC; tumors with high PKC-alpha dependence should be more sensitive
PKC-eta is upregulated in the virtual-cell response to SC-9, suggesting PKC-family signaling mediates sensitivity
NOTCH1-mutant KYSE270 is sensitive; NOTCH1 is upregulated in the virtual-cell response
NF1 loss (BICR6, FTC133, KALS1, LOXIMVI) activates RAS/PKC signaling in sensitive lines
